cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Outsmart the Room
cards.instruction: Turn every clue, deduction, and secret into a contest you must solve or control first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't announce where the office biscuits are yet. I haven't finished checking the delivery record.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Reception has the box. I'm going down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A box is not an identification. Bring it here unopened and I'll establish the contents.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've opened it. They're eating them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then ask which biscuits. Precisely. Nobody calls this solved before I've checked it against the order.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 withholds announcement pending A's check. A3 corrects B2's box-as-solution and A5 corrects B4's eating-as-proof to keep every step under A's own verification.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 location would solve the search, so A3 moves to contents; B4 eating resolves contents, causing A5 a still narrower identity-versus-order test.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants to retrieve the biscuits and B4 reports colleagues already eating. Their ordinary priorities contrast naturally with A's exaggerated competitive investigation.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's apparent completion to invent another necessary check that only A may finish, extending control without new objects.

specificity.evidence: A1 office delivery, B2 reception and B4 opened box/eating give a clear trivial mystery and why others move faster.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's precise question and no-one-calls-it-solved instruction express competitive control directly to B rather than describing it for a reviewer.
